To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated a Yb-dopped hybrid fiber with anomolus dispersion near 1 µm that allows for high peak power femtosecond pulses to be generated.

we demonstrate a Yb hybrid fiber with a sharp dispersion peak near 1.06 μm, and that we use it for the first time to nonlinearly compress 1 ps wideband pulses to 90 fs, which is to the best of knowledge the best all-fiber system operating near 1 μm.

the hybrid fiber with a sharp dispersion peak allows us to compress pulses down to 90 fs with a power of 10 kW in an all-fiber setup, and that the operation near the dispersion peak is found to be most optimal for the compression.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we demonstrate the first hybrid fiber with anomally dispersion in the 1000 nm spectral range, where single mode behavior is achieved with differential mode amplification, and we demonstrate that this fiber can be used for nonlinear chirped pulse amplification to generate high-peak-power, high-quality, and femtosecond pulses.
the Yb-doped anomalous-dispersion hybrid fiber with the differential mode amplification is an excellent candidate for high-peak-power, all-fiber femtosecond laser systems operating near 1050 nm.
the hybrid fiber is a promising candidate for the generation of high-power femtoseond pulses near 1 µm, and it is particularly suitable for the compression of broadband pulses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrate high-peak power femtosecond laser sources in the 1 μm spectral range based on nonlinear chirped pulse amplification in an all-fiber laser architecture.
we have developed a new fiber design for high-power nonlinear chirped-pulse compression, which is based on a hybrid fiber with a large mode field diameter, and a sharp dispersion slope peak.
the Yb-doped fiber with a sharp dispersion peak can provide an effective means to generate high-peak-power ultrashort laser pulses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid fiber is a promising candidate for high-peak-power, all-fiber chirped pulse amplification systems operating near 1000 nm, where it can be used for both pulse compression and amplification.
the dispersion properties of the hybrid fiber can be tailored to achieve optimal pulse compression in both the spectral regions of anomalous and normal dispersion.

the combination of the hybrid mode field profile and the sharp dispersion peak allows for efficient nonlinear pulse compression in the 1 μm spectral range, which is of interest for a wide range of applications.
